transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-03
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alyssa Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Marquez (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Halcyon CTO), Ethan Lowe (ML Eng), Marta Ruiz (Security)

Summary (auto): Quick scoping on models and infra options. High interest in long context models, tool-calling integration to internal APIs, and private/VPC deployment for regulated telemetry data.

00:00 Priya Nair: okay thanks everyone for joining, we've got about 50 minutes. Priya here, I'm the CTO at Halcyon. We mainly build fleet telemetry and analytics for shipping — lots of long documents, logs, multi-lingual operator notes.
00:15 Alyssa Chen: thanks Priya, I'm Alyssa from Redwood, i'll run quick intro and hand off to Diego for the deep stuff. little background — we help run inference in hosted/dedicated/private modes.
00:34 Diego Marquez: hey all, diego here, i'll dig into the technical trade offs — latency, cost, context, kv cache and tool-calling. quick question for Ethan: what are your typical prompt sizes and are you expecting 8k or 32k windows?
00:48 Ethan Lowe: um yeah good q. Most of our runs start around 2–4k tokens but then for incident reconstructions we want to stitch whole session logs so those can go up to 25–30k tokens. so realistically we need 32k compatibility or smart chunking that preserves context across calls.
01:10 Priya Nair: and importantly, the model needs to handle English, Spanish, Portuguese — operator notes are mainly those three. also we have a couple of internal structured tools that the LLM should call to fetch exact telemetry rows, so tool-calling + structured outputs are important.
01:32 Marta Ruiz: from security side we'll need VPC + customer-managed keys, audit logs with retention, and SSO (SAML). we also need to know where tokens are stored and how long logs retained.
01:47 Alyssa Chen: totally, that's a common set. quick orientation: Hosted is fastest to get started — we run in our managed infra; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput; Private gives you the private control plane and on-prem options with KMS. Diego — maybe walk through model choices for long context and multilingual?
02:10 Diego Marquez: sure. in the open-model space there are big families with different context limits. You can run a model natively at 32k if it's architected for it, or use windowing plus persistent KV cache to approximate longer memory. For multilingual, some LLM weights are better trained on non-English corpora. There's also the tuning/LoRA path for custom data. A couple of practical tradeoffs: 32k mode is more expensive per token and sometimes needs larger GPU types; quantized 8-bit runtimes can help on cost but some 32k kernels are less optimized today.
03:05 Ethan Lowe: when you say KV cache, do you mean we can append embeddings or summaries to keep a running memory without resending full logs? that's interesting.
03:17 Diego Marquez: exactly. Redwood's runtime has prefix / KV cache strategies: you can cache past key/value states for tokens so you don't retransmit everything each time. also we do intelligent prefix summarization suggestions — basically summarize older context and store as shorter prompts. it's a tradeoff vs freshness.
03:40 Priya Nair: does that work across model upgrades? we might want to change models mid-rollout.
03:48 Diego Marquez: good question — we version caches per model family. we also have fallback policies so if the preferred model is unavailable we can route to a compatible variant. but you should plan a cache warm-up when changing model families.
04:05 Marta Ruiz: and for Private, do you support HSM-backed KMS or only cloud KMS?
04:13 Alyssa Chen: Private supports customer-provided KMS integrations and HSM in some on-prem packages; we can share the compliance checklist.
04:23 Priya Nair: on multilingual — have you benchmarked Spanish/Portuguese quality across the open models?
04:31 Diego Marquez: yes, we have bench results at a high-level. some open models trained on multilingual corpora (e.g., certain Llama-family forks and Mistral variants) do much better. but there's wide variance and often the right move is a small fine-tune or RLHF-like calibration with your own operator transcripts. we can run a focused eval with your prompt set.
04:57 Ethan Lowe: that's the key. we'll share a representative set — both short queries and the long incident reconstructions.
05:08 Diego Marquez: perfect. regarding tool-calling: Redwood supports function-style/tool calling (structured output) and we can connect to internal APIs via secure connectors; in hosted we do proxying with tokenization policies, in private you can host connectors inside your VPC. Some customers prefer dedicated for lower latency when calling internal services.
05:38 Priya Nair: latency is a concern; many of our operator flows are interactive, sub-300ms is nice but not mandatory. what latency numbers do you expect at 8k vs 32k?
05:51 Diego Marquez: ballpark — for generation workloads at 8k on dedicated GPUs we often see tail latencies in the low hundreds ms for short responses, but for 32k context it's more variable; think 1–3s depending on output length and batching. Hosted can be similar but depends on plan and queueing; Dedicated gives more predictable p50/p95 because of reserved pools. We'll produce a more detailed latency spreadsheet after we see your prompt set and concurrency assumptions.
06:25 Ethan Lowe: about concurrency — for incident triage we have bursts: maybe 50 concurrent users during peak. how does Redwood handle concurrency + batching without exploding latency?
06:35 Diego Marquez: our runtime uses continuous batching and adaptive batching windows. you can tune max batch size and latency SLOs; Dedicated allows larger reserved capacity so bursts are absorbed. We also offer autoscaling and burst capacity add-ons. There's also a 'cost-aware routing' feature to route non-critical requests to cheaper model variants.
07:02 Priya Nair: curious about cost — any rough TCO numbers for hosted 32k vs dedicated?
07:09 Alyssa Chen: we'll do exact math later, but we typically show customers that dedicated becomes more economical above predictable sustained throughput (X tokens/month). for bursty loads hosted might be cheaper initially. we'll send a model-cost spreadsheet.
07:25 Marta Ruiz: we need data residency info — some telemetry originates in EU, and some in LATAM. Residency controls and regional routing are important.
07:33 Diego Marquez: regional routing is supported; you can pin requests to regions and we can enforce data residency policies. For Private you can fully isolate in a customer's region or on-prem.
07:47 Ethan Lowe: on-tool calling, is there a dry-run or simulation mode? we want to test without touching prod APIs.
07:55 Diego Marquez: yes, sandbox connectors and mock endpoints are common. You can also do function call responses as structured JSON without executing downstream calls.
08:08 Priya Nair: what about eval and regression detection? we need to ensure model upgrades don't regress on key prompts.
08:16 Alyssa Chen: Redwood Optimize and the eval hooks let you run prompt sets continuously and alert on quality regressions. we tie alerts to rollout policies so you can auto-rollback. sometimes the telemetry names were transcribed oddly — sorry 'Redwood Optimist' in the past, the transcript may mis-say it — but it's Redwood Optimize.
08:35 Ethan Lowe: ha, understood. can you talk about quantization and which models maintain quality when quantized for cost savings?
08:44 Diego Marquez: quantization is model-specific. many Llama-derivatives and some newer families quantize well to 4-bit/8-bit with minimal quality loss; however for some multilingual and long-context kernels you need to validate. quantization may affect numeric stability in long attention. It's another reason to run a sample benchmark.
09:15 Priya Nair: do you have customers in regulated sectors doing Private deployments for telemetry?
09:20 Alyssa Chen: yes, several telco and industrial customers run Private with customer-managed KMS and on-prem connectors. We'll share sanitized architecture diagrams and the compliance pack.
09:36 Marta Ruiz: about audit logs — we need immutable logs with at least 3 months retention and ability to export to our SIEM.
09:44 Diego Marquez: supported — audit logs can be exported and we support log-forwarding to customer endpoints; retention is configurable on Dedicated/Private.
10:00 Ethan Lowe: ok, technical curiosity — if we pick an open 32k model, what GPU footprint are we looking at? gpus, memory?
10:08 Diego Marquez: for native 32k you typically use A100/GBs or next-gen L40-like instances; memory and kernel support matter. Some inference optimizations reduce memory with kv offload and quantization but throughput is lower. If you want numbers we can map model -> GPU type -> tokens/sec in the spreadsheet.
10:36 Priya Nair: about model updates: if we fine-tune on our transcripts, how is that served? are we hosting custom weights?
10:45 Diego Marquez: options: host tuned weights in Redwood (hosted or dedicated) or in Private you can keep weights in your environment. We support pinned model versions and can roll out with canaries. For some customers we host adapted checkpoints with access controls.
11:05 Ethan Lowe: we'd probably want a small LoRA or fine-tune for operator lingo.
11:10 Diego Marquez: that's a common approach. small LoRA can be cheap and effective. We can run calibration evals before and after.
11:25 Priya Nair: any gotchas with streaming responses for tool-calling? we need partial outputs quickly to power UI.
11:34 Diego Marquez: streaming is supported; tool-calling with streaming sometimes needs careful framing to avoid midstream function calls — we recommend staged outputs: first structured tool call token, then stream answer. It's an engineering detail we can help design.
11:58 Marta Ruiz: I'd like to see the security questionnaire and network diagrams.
12:05 Alyssa Chen: we'll attach those in follow-up.
12:12 Ethan Lowe: about region latency — we have users in São Paulo and Lisbon; any experience with routing to avoid cross-region hops?
12:21 Diego Marquez: pick nearest region, and we can set routing policies to prefer SA/EU endpoints, plus fallbacks. For Private you can place infra in those regions.
12:36 Priya Nair: can Redwood do cost-aware routing by model family for different flows? like critical triage hits expensive model, background indexing hits cheaper model.
12:44 Diego Marquez: yep that's exactly a use case for our smart routing and traffic policies. You can set route by priority, latency SLO, or cost target.
13:02 Ethan Lowe: what's the recommended pilot? we want to validate 32k incident stitching, tool-calling to mock APIs, and multilingual quality on Spanish/Portuguese.
13:12 Alyssa Chen: recommended pilot: 2–4 week focused pilot on Hosted or Dedicated dev pool: you provide prompt set, we run benchmarks (latency, cost, quality), run a tool-calling mock integration, and produce a plan for Dedicated or Private deployment. We'll include SOC2 docs.
13:34 Priya Nair: timeline wise, we want a pilot early Feb. can we have the benchmark results within a week after sample prompts?
13:42 Diego Marquez: yes that's doable if we get the prompt set and payloads by Monday.
13:50 Ethan Lowe: we'll share prompts and sample logs by Monday (Feb 8) — action: Ethan to send.
14:00 Alyssa Chen: perfect. last call: any blockers on your side?
14:06 Marta Ruiz: need legal to review pilot terms and confirm data handling. we'll coordinate.
14:12 Priya Nair: also, small note: we have an internal bias/op interpretability requirement — we might want explainability hooks.
14:20 Diego Marquez: we have tracing and token-level attribution and eval tools that can help. not perfect but useful.
14:33 Alyssa Chen: recap / next steps: 1) Ethan shares prompts and sample payloads; 2) Diego runs perf/cost estimates for hosted vs dedicated at 8k/32k and shares spreadsheet; 3) Alyssa sends pilot pricing and SOC2/compliance pack; 4) Marta/legal to review terms. we'll schedule benchmark session week of Feb 8.
14:58 Priya Nair: thanks all — that's helpful. we'll be in touch.
15:05 Alyssa Chen: thanks everyone, end.
notes: Transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., 'Redwood Optimist'). References to GPUs are approximate; exact sizing will come from benchmarking. Customer expressed strong preference for pilot to validate 32k stitching + tool-calling in a sandbox before committing to Dedicated or Private.
